question: In December 2021, which of the following countries announced that it will no longer censor films released in cinemas, the country's latest effort to boost its brand as a liberal hub attractive to foreigners?
solution:
The correct answer is __**United Arab Emirates**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The United Arab Emirates (UAE) **has announced that cinematic films would no longer be censored.
 
• It's seen as part of the kingdom's aim to improve its image as a liberal hotspot that attracts visitors from around the world.
 
• "The films will be played in theatres in accordance with their international version," according to the authorities.
 
• The government is changing its Islamic legal system, and beginning next year, the weekend will be changed to Saturday-Sunday.
 
• In the federation of seven sheikhdoms, foreigners outnumber locals by about nine to one.
 
• The tourism-dependent country's mix of culture and religion has at times clashed with** its Islamic laws and traditions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **United Arab Emirates:**

 
 
• Capital: Abu Dhabi
 
• Largest city: Dubai
 
• Official languages: Arabic
 
• President: Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan
